svg.text: Complete class diagram (detailed): IO, logic, AI and data layers
Combines diagrams 03 to 07. Entity classes map to the database tables listed in the note at the bottom.
Repository<T> is the abstract parent. Each subclass stores one entity: User, LegalReference, Analysis, ClauseComment.
All four enumerations extend ChoiceEnum (str, Enum), which gives them one shared _parse().
Deleting an Analysis deletes its Clauses, ClauseReferences and ClauseComments. LegalReferences are shared and stay.
Review feature: PUT / DELETE /api/admin/analyses/<id>/clauses/<n>/comment, both wrapped by _admin_required (server-side check).
ADMIN_USERNAME / ADMIN_PASSWORD (.env) become an admin at start-up (AuthService.seed_admin_from_env). Customers only read the comment.
Database tables (PostgreSQL, created from the entities): users, analyses, clauses, clause_comments, clause_references, legal_references.
Keys: analyses.owner_id -> users.id; clauses.analysis_id -> analyses.id (cascade); clause_comments.clause_id -> clauses.id (cascade, unique) and author_id -> users.id;
clause_references (clause_id, reference_id) is the join table to legal_references. Unique: users.username, legal_references.url, clauses(analysis_id, position).
Ids are readable (us_001, an_001, cm_001) from sequences; check constraints limit role, status, risk_level and verification to the enumeration values.
